Simulate and Estimate Markov Chain Functionals

Source: R/05_parallel.R
estim_parallel.Rd

Simulate independent trajectories, fit a Markov chain to each trajectory, and apply a function to each fit.

Usage

estim_parallel(x, fun, k = 1000, m = 500, ..., n_workers = 2L)

Arguments

x

A MarkovChain object.

fun

A function accepting a fitted MarkovChain as argument x.

k

A positive integer giving the number of trajectories.

m

An integer of at least two giving the number of states observed per trajectory (m - 1 transitions).

...

Additional arguments passed to fun.

n_workers

A positive integer giving the maximum number of PSOCK workers. Set to one for sequential execution.

Value

The results of fun combined with c() in simulation order. For one trajectory, the result of fun is returned directly.

Details

Each fit estimates the transition matrix with fit() and retains the initial distribution from x. An error is raised if any trajectory omits a state, because the fit would have a smaller state space. Choose a trajectory length that gives adequate coverage of the states.

Use set.seed() before calling this function for reproducible simulations with a fixed worker count. For parallel execution, fun and its arguments must be usable in a fresh R session with the package installed.

See also

sim(), fit()

Examples

P <- matrix(c(0.8, 0.2, 0.3, 0.7), nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE)
x <- MarkovChain(c(1, 0), P)
set.seed(1)
estim_parallel(x, mttf, k = 4, m = 200, up = 1, n_workers = 1)
#> [1] 5.000000 5.619048 4.346154 4.360000
